statement.p: Evaluate \int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} f(x,y,z)\,dV for the function f and region \mathcal{W} specified:

p.me: f(x,y,z)=42(x+y)\quad \mathcal{W}: y\le z \le x, 0\le y\le x , 0\le x\le 1

static.solution:
\mathcal{W} is the region between the planes z=y and z=x lying over the triangle \mathcal{D} in the xy-plane defined by
the inequalities 0\le y\le x, 0\le x\le 1.
We compute the integral, using Theorem 2, by evaluating the following iterated integral:
\begin{array}{rcl} \int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} (42(x+y) ) \,dV \amp =\amp \int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}}\left(\int_{y}^{x}( 42(x+y) ) \,dz\right)\,dA\\ \amp =\amp \int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}} (42(x+y) )z\bigg|_{z=y}^{x}dA= \int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}} 42( x+y )( x-y ) \,dA\\ \amp =\amp \int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}} 42\left({x}^2-{y}^2\right) \,dA= \int_0^1 \int_0^{x} 42\left({x}^2-{y}^2\right)dy \,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^1 \left(\int_0^{x} 42\left({x}^2-{y}^2\right) \,dy\right) \,dx= \int_0^1 42\left({x}^2y-\frac{{y}^3}{3}\right) \bigg|_{y=0}^{x}dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^1 28x^3 \,dx= 7 x^4 \bigg|_0^1= 7 \end{array}
